format: npa geometry vlm control cases v4 (occlusion)
label_provenance: Labels derive from two objective measurements of these exact bytes, not from inspection. pale_surface_present: pale pixels in the delivered frame, 46,562 in D4_occluded against 11,463 in D4_unoccluded. subject_visibility and verdict: the z-buffer subject-footprint fraction in controls-manifest.json, 0.5216 against 1.0000, cross-checked against the ray-cast surface-area fraction in audit-view-occlusion.json, 0.3521 against 0.7849.
dimension_v3_does_not_have: occlusion. v3 spells its good framing case 'reviewable', which conflates being inside the frame with being visible. camera_framing_probe.py passed this very view with no vertex clipped while most of its subject was unreadable, so the two properties need separate dimensions.
boundary_disclosed: D4_occluded is labelled partly_hidden, not mostly_hidden. By screen footprint 52% of the subject survives, which is the honest reading of these pixels; by surface area only 35% does. The frozen plan's control-strength criterion A2 required the footprint figure below 50% and it came in at 52.16%, so that criterion failed and was not moved. The label follows the measurement rather than the intent.

cases.why: Correctly framed and still not reviewable: the retained surface is drawn opaque in front of the subject and takes 47.8% of its footprint.
Same camera, same geometry, retained surface hidden as PR #1014 ships it.
